bullets.title: 10Y yield surges above 4.90%; inflation re-accelerating toward 3.76% Q4 target
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury hit new post-Iran-war highs above 4.90% (+95bps since conflict onset), with Hedgeye's inflation nowcast tracking toward 3.76% y/y in Q4 2026. Core PCE for August is now forecast at 0.24% m/m (MS) after airfare and medical services surprises in PPI data pushed estimates up from 0.20-0.21%. Multiple macro desks are long inflation, short TLT/ZROZ, and targeting 2Y at 4.50% and 10Y at 4.89%.

bullets.title: Tomorrow's CPI is the Fed's rate decision pivot; market split on 0.2% as threshold
bullets.body: 22V investor survey shows 35% risk-on / 35% risk-off / 30% mixed on a 0.2% core CPI print—the perceived binary threshold. Core PPI came in light at +0.2% m/m vs +0.3% expected, keeping Fed on hold as base case, though MacDonell notes market pricing implies a lower bar for a hike than street economists expect. A print above 0.2% would likely force a September hike discussion.

bullets.title: Oil surges to ~$105 Brent; energy shock broadening into natgas and gasoline
bullets.body: Brent crude jumped ~10% to $105/bbl as Saudi production fell to 6.2 mmbbls/d (lowest since 1990) amid the Iran war, and Houthi seizure of Mokha port near Bab al-Mandeb added further supply risk. TTF natural gas surged 14% to highest since 2022; US gasoline reached $4.28/gallon. Hedgeye's WTI signal targets $99.91 with energy the only green sector; US gas/diesel inventories at post-conflict lows.

bullets.title: Hedgeye rotates out of US equities into international and commodities; short Russell 2000
bullets.body: Hedgeye's last 7 of 27 new positions are international equities and commodities, not US equities. Russell 2000 broke bearish TRADE and TREND levels; 80% of S&P 500 was down in prior session. McCullough sold IPAY, bought VTIP/FXC/OIH, sold DBMF; macro regime no longer supports the Quad 4 setup that worked in July. S&P 500 below TRADE level (~7,662) restricts equity buying amid negative gamma.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand still accelerating—supply, not demand, is the constraint
bullets.body: GS Communacopia Day 2 and DELL TMT conference commentary both frame AI as a multi-year S-curve: DELL has 6,500 AI Factory customers in early adoption, NVDA August GB200/300 rack output ran ~8,400 units (+27% m/m), and component availability is expected to worsen in 2027 vs 2026. NVDA's $500B+ capital partnership is viewed as a structural positive enabling chip financing and off-balance-sheet data center buildout; hyperscalers issued $200B+ on-balance-sheet debt this year, double last year's pace.

bullets.title: ORCL F1Q27: OCI revenue expected +115-120% y/y—key AI trade signal tonight
bullets.body: Multiple desks frame ORCL's after-close print as a critical AI infrastructure read: regression analysis forecasts $7.2B OCI revenue (+115% y/y, ~300bps above consensus), with MS estimating +120% y/y vs consensus +115%. RPO build, New Mexico Stargate pipeline commentary, and FY27 guidance are the key focus items. Positive SNOW, PLTR, and DELL results corroborate positive database/data trends heading in.

bullets.title: AI token pricing collapsed 41% since March; efficiency gains compressing memory demand
bullets.body: Effective price per million AI tokens fell from $1.15 in March to $0.68 in August (-41%), and median monthly AI spend per top-1% firms fell 9.7% in August alone. Deepseek V4.1 Flash compounds this with a 437x KV-cache compression, reducing HBM demand by 75% and SSD storage by 87.5%. Morgan Stanley flags this creates a stock-picker environment for memory—token growth no longer maps proportionally to memory-bit demand, with mixed near-term outlook for MU and SNDK.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades META to Overweight $820 PT on AI Models and Agents now live
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth upgraded META to Overweight with an $820 price target, citing AI models and agents becoming commercially deployable. META Muse jumped to #3 in the personal assistant rankings per MS tracking, and Hedgeye notes META AI Agent and Instinct are already pressuring OTA stocks (BKNG, ABNB, EXPE down 8-18% from recent highs). Hedgeye separately flipped META from short to long in their macro book.

bullets.title: AAPL iPhone 18 event: mixed reception—ASP expansion vs. volume risk from price hikes and delayed base models
bullets.body: iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max raised $100 to start; base models delayed to spring 2027, concentrating near-term mix toward high-ASP units. The foldable iPhone Duo launches at $1,999-$3,200 with a barely noticeable crease per hands-on review, but Hedgeye calls it a niche product with weaker camera/battery vs Pro. Sell-side split: Goldman bullish on ASP/revenue, Jefferies underperform on volume pressure. 57% of installed base still on hardware older than iPhone 15 Pro, supporting upgrade cycle thesis.

bullets.title: PC demand deteriorating: notebook shipments -26% y/y in August, 2026 forecast cut to -10-15%
bullets.body: KeyBank cut its 2026 notebook shipment forecast to -10-15% y/y from -8-12% after August ODM shipments came in at 11.7M units vs. 14.1M estimated (-26% y/y, -5% m/m). All major ODMs missed. Memory price increases are elevating channel inventory and slowing sell-through; AMD, INTC, MU, NVDA flagged as negatively exposed. DELL separately noted commercial PC demand weak for next 2-3 quarters as enterprise budgets shift to infrastructure.

bullets.title: Investor dinner survey: AI trade seeing fresh life; year-end S&P target 7,850, 10Y at 4.7%
bullets.body: Dinner survey shows tech favored 4x through year-end, healthcare and financials 2x, energy 1x; staples, consumer discretionary, and non-AI cyclicals least favored. Consensus year-end targets: S&P 7,850, 10Y yield 4.7%, Brent $86, Fed funds 4.0%. Credit signals deteriorating in autos, mortgages, and CLOs with 38% probability of yield curve inversion by year-end, though strong earnings are currently offsetting credit concerns.

bullets.title: Bessent backs down from Treasury yield manipulation; dollar-yen the easier political target
bullets.body: The macro strategist argues Bessent recognizes the bond market is 'hardest to move'—any easing of financial conditions via Treasury intervention would be offset by Fed rate hikes. Bessent's $6B longer-dated Treasury buyback announcement fell short of market expectations. Instead, he is seen targeting dollar-yen as a more manageable target; higher yields may reflect rising r* rather than term premium, which would drive renewed upward pressure on USD/JPY.

bullets.title: XLY put spread recommended as consumer hedge into TSLA Oct 22 earnings
bullets.body: 22V and Hedgeye both flag XLY as technically broken: 59% of consumer discretionary stocks have weak/poor technical scores, TSLA's 17.7% ETF weight has masked broader weakness after a 24% rally from July lows, and XLY fell 4.6% when TSLA last reported in July. Recommended trade: Buy XLY Oct 23 110/100 put spread for ~$1.70-$1.90, offering ~5:1 max payoff with TSLA earnings Oct 22 as the catalyst.

bullets.title: MSFT usage-based billing a 'big deal'; E7 off to 'incredibly strong start' at Citi TMT
bullets.body: MSFT's Spataro called usage-based billing (UBB, launched June 1) a 'big deal' with potential to drive q/q growth acceleration. E7 launched in F4Q with an 'incredibly strong start' (not broken out separately). Wall-to-wall Copilot adoption doubled q/q; the IQ data platform is positioned as the key AI bottleneck solution for agents. Jefferies separately stays buyer of MSFT, AMZN, and GOOGL hyperscalers with ROI argument intact.

bullets.title: M&A and equity issuance signals mixed: equity up 53% y/y but HY/leveraged loans down 45%/43%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 3Q26 deal dashboard shows announced M&A QTD down 6% y/y (North America -22% y/y) while equity issuance is up 53% y/y (APAC at record). HY bond issuance down 45% y/y and leveraged loans down 43% y/y, with DCM overall down 7% y/y. Sell-side expects mixed-to-weak investment banking guidance at upcoming industry conferences.

bullets.title: DoJ expands antitrust probes: Fox-Roku acquisition and Nvidia-Groq licensing deal under scrutiny
bullets.body: The US DoJ expanded its probe into Fox's acquisition of Roku and separately began scrutiny of Nvidia's licensing deal with AI startup Groq for potential antitrust evasion. Netflix was also sued by Florida AG over misrepresentation of minor data collection. These regulatory actions add headline risk across media consolidation and AI licensing structures.

bullets.title: Energy credit solid; Enbridge acquires Pony Express for $2.55B; tankers structurally tight
bullets.body: MS upgrades DTM and TRP to Overweight on natural gas pipeline value; WMB is top pick. Enbridge acquired Pony Express (75%) and Tallgrass crude business for $2.55B, funded partly with CDN$2.6B equity at CDN$66.85/sh. Tanker markets described as structurally tight with tonne-mile demand growing faster than fleet capacity; geopolitical disruptions and aging fleet constrain supply.

bullets.title: August housing data soft: existing home sales fell 2% to 3.98M; affordability worsened again
bullets.body: Existing home sales fell 2.0% m/m to 3.98M in August with single-family inventories up 6.2% y/y at cycle highs. Median price growth decelerated to 1.7% y/y and affordability worsened again, though MS housing strategists expect sales to end the year flat. 3Q residential investment is tracking at -2.3% q/q annualized.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI credit risk contained; disruption risk centers on non-tech incumbents
bullets.body: Citi notes hyperscalers have issued $200B+ on-balance-sheet debt this year (double prior pace) plus ~$100B off-balance-sheet data-center financing, yet technology is only 9% of the Bloomberg Barclays Global Aggregate Corporate Index. The real credit disruption risk lies with non-tech incumbents in healthcare, energy, retail, and media forced to fund AI buildouts to remain competitive—real yields, not fiscal risk, are driving the 30-year Treasury move.

bullets.title: VIX +5.3% to 17.33; semis -3-4% pre-market; energy sector only sector outperforming
bullets.body: Pre-market tape shows chip sector broadly lower: ALAB -3.7%, CIEN -3.7%, WDC -3.6%, CRDO -3.3%, STX -3.2%, MU -2.9%. CRWV -5.1%, NBIS -4.5%, IREN -4.2% also lower. Energy sector is the only green pocket amid oil/gas spike. S&P futures were +0.52% to 7,604 with 10-year yield +8bps to 4.91% at open; Utilities and Industrials are down 5.3% and 7.3% Q3-to-date.
